acridine as a simple, readily available ligand promotes an aerobic oxidative dehydrohydrogenative coupling between nonbiased olefns and arenes, providing a broad range of alkenyl arenes in good yields under ambient pressure of air.
the direct C-H aryation of nonbiased olefin is achieved by the use of a simple ligand and ambient oxygen pressure.
a new biomimetic aerobic dehydrogenative coupling of arenes and nonfunctionalized olefins has been developed, which proceeds under ambient oxygen pressure.

the development of novel and efficient methods for the direct C-H aryation of alkenes.
the development of new synthetic methods for the preparation of alkenylated arenes.
the development of new methods for the direct C-H aryation of nonbiased olefin.

the reaction is a ligand promoted aerobic dehydrogenative C-H cross coupling between arenes and olefins.
the acridine ligand promotes the oxidative dehydrogenation of the olefin and the oxidative dehydrocoupling of the arene in an efficient biomimetic aerobic process.

acridine is a powerful ligand for aerobic direct C–H arylation of nonactivated alkenes.
